narrative.summary: In the quiet village of Little Middleton, the discovery of a forged excavation report leads to the murder of landowner Beatrice Dunmore. The community is shaken when the trusted dig supervisor, Ambrose Rutherford, is implicated through a complex web of archival deception exploiting the unquestioned authority of official records. Frances Orme, a determined local detective, unravels the truth by exposing the forgery and revealing how social authority was manipulated to conceal the crime.

accepted_facts: Beatrice Dunmore was found dead, stabbed with an ornate letter opener belonging to Ambrose Rutherford.
A forged excavation report falsely dated weeks before the murder was accepted as official.
The archival stamps on the excavation report are in an unusual sequence.
The watermark on the report's paper dates to six months after the claimed date of the report.
Ambrose was the only person with access and motive to forge the report.
Frances Orme has uncovered discrepancies in the archival documents.
inferred_conclusions: The official excavation report was deliberately forged to mislead the village and authorities.
Ambrose Rutherford manipulated the archival records to protect his position and conceal the true timing of the dig's findings.
Beatrice Dunmore discovered the forgery and was murdered to silence her.
The social authority of Ambrose and the archival system was exploited to delay suspicion and investigation.

mechanism.description: Ambrose Rutherford forged the date on the official excavation report by chemically aging the ink to simulate natural oxidation. He exploited the unquestioned authority of the archival system and the social hierarchy that accepted documents without thorough verification. The report's true paper watermark and archival stamps reveal the forgery. This manipulation delayed suspicion, allowing Ambrose to commit the murder and create a false timeline to support his alibi.

delivery_path.step: Ambrose obtained blank archival paper with a watermark dated six months after the forged report's claimed date.
He chemically treated the ink to simulate natural aging and oxidation typical of older documents.
Ambrose inserted the forged report into the archival system, manipulating the order of archival stamps.
The village elders and officials accepted the report's authority without cross-verifying paper watermarks or stamp sequences.
Beatrice Dunmore discovered discrepancies and confronted Ambrose, who murdered her using his letter opener.

outcome.result: The forged report created a false timeline, giving Ambrose an alibi during the apparent time of death. Once Frances Orme reveals the forgery and exposes the archival irregularities, Ambrose's deception collapses, and he is identified as the murderer.

false_assumption.statement: The official excavation report's date and archival stamps are accurate and can be trusted as proof of the timeline.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The report is issued under the dig supervisor's authority and bears official archival stamps, which villagers and officials accept without question due to social hierarchy and trust in archival procedures.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It hides the forgery of the report's date, the manipulation of archival stamps, and the true timeline of events that contradict Ambrose Rutherford's alibi.

supporting_points: Desmond had a public quarrel with Ambrose and was seen near the dig site around the time of Beatrice's death.
His alibi is weak, and he had motive to want the dig funding to collapse.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: Desmond's alibi during the actual time of death is confirmed by multiple villagers in the pub, and he had no access to the letter opener or the archival documents.

red_herrings.description: A glove mark found on the letter opener in the dig site office matches Ottoline Thorne.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Ottoline handled the letter opener while cataloguing documents earlier in the day, with no knowledge of the murder.

red_herrings.description: A witness claims to have seen Josephine Whitlock near the archives room at the time the forged report was supposedly filed.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Josephine was performing routine archival duties unrelated to the forgery, unaware of any manipulation.

closed_circle.rationale: All suspects were present in the village with access to the dig site or archives. No outsiders could reach the village or the victim unnoticed due to isolation and strict social controls.

discriminating_test.design: Reexamine the official excavation report under controlled archival conditions, comparing the paper watermark date and archival stamp sequence with known filing protocols and chemical ink aging tests. This exposes the forgery by demonstrating the impossibility of the stated date and the manipulated archival stamps, directly contradicting Ambrose Rutherford's alibi and official authority.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test reveals the report's forgery through physical and procedural contradictions, disproving Ambrose's timeline and implicating him in the murder.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The archival experts confirm the chemical aging and stamp manipulation, invalidating the report's authenticity and collapsing Ambrose's alibi.

fair_play.explanation: Step 1: The fresh handling mark on the letter opener and restricted access to the dig office (constraint_space.access) allow the reader to narrow the weapon's handler early. Step 2: The watermark dating and report location clues (constraint_space.physical and time anchors) are presented mid-case to expose the forgery. Step 3: The archival stamp order anomaly (constraint_space.physical.traces) is clearly described before the test. Step 4: The unique access and knowledge of Ambrose Rutherford are established early to satisfy the means-link. All necessary clues appear before the discriminating test scene.
